# Vendored SDL3 dependencies

The SDL dependencies are official upstream git submodules pinned to released
revisions:

- SDL 3.4.14
- SDL_image 3.4.4
- SDL_ttf 3.2.2

The gitlinks are the authoritative revision pins.  `build.sh` verifies the
installed pkg-config versions so that a partially updated dependency set
cannot be used accidentally.

## Build contract

Initialize the submodules during source preparation, before starting an
offline or network-isolated build:

```sh
git submodule update --init vendor/sdl3/SDL \
    vendor/sdl3/SDL_image vendor/sdl3/SDL_ttf
```

Build and install the dependencies into private, absolute paths:

```sh
vendor/sdl3/build.sh \
    --build-dir=/absolute/path/to/sdl3-build \
    --prefix=/absolute/path/to/sdl3-prefix
```

The build produces static SDL3, SDL3_image, and SDL3_ttf libraries.  It uses
the platform's codec, FreeType, and HarfBuzz development packages and never
downloads CMake dependencies.  The build directory and prefix must differ.
They must not be shared by different target platforms.

Configure XPilot Infinity against that exact prefix with:

```sh
./configure --with-sdl3=vendored \
    --with-sdl3-prefix=/absolute/path/to/sdl3-prefix
```

`--with-sdl3=system` remains the default and uses the normal pkg-config search
path.  Neither option removes or changes the existing platform clients; it
only selects the SDL3 dependency provider when the SDL client is enabled.

For cross-compilation, pass an absolute CMake toolchain file to `build.sh`:

```sh
vendor/sdl3/build.sh \
    --build-dir=/absolute/path/to/target-sdl3-build \
    --prefix=/absolute/path/to/target-sdl3-prefix \
    --toolchain-file=/absolute/path/to/toolchain.cmake
```

This separation is intentional for future container and package builds.  A
source-preparation stage can materialize the pinned submodules, while each
platform container owns its dependency build, prefix, and XPilot Infinity build
directory.  Debian packaging and container definitions are outside this
directory and are not generated by this script.
